Answer: C
Reason: The frontal view (Figure 1a) shows a large, well-defined mass in the right paracardiac region with visible internal calcifications. The lateral view (Figure 1b) localizes this mass to the anterior mediastinum (retrosternal space), which, combined with the presence of calcification, is highly characteristic of a thymoma (or potentially a teratoma, but thymoma is the best fit among the choices for an anterior calcified mass).
